touches.text: A node id is its master row number and never anything else (Akien, Q#104, 2026-11-14). WHY: any other lookup needs a search, and a row id is direct; a search is far too slow on the target hardware. A node can be voided and its row reused; a node is never searched for.
Proofs run against a TESTING database, separate from live.

trees: leaf tables keep their shape and weights. A leaf points at a node address, and the node's in list holds the leaf's address back. So each leaf table gains an additive row bigint column and keeps leaf_id, and its table tag is assigned at its birth from a tag registry the home librarian holds (0x0100 upward, synced like nodes); tags.json pins only the core four (CC, a mechanism under Q#108, 2026-11-14).
The only way to the database. WHY: the authentication is wrapped up in it, and every table has exactly one owner who gates every write; an ownerless table can't be made (Postgres refuses it).
Publishes a client tool (connect, read, write, query ...) that talks to the database over its socket, no bus hop: faster (2.3.7.1.1).
scratch: a proof's throwaway temp dirs and worktrees, cleaned up by the door. WHY: a run must leave nothing behind (4.3.1.7). USERS: the tester.
